source.title: Automatic Jailbreaking of the Text-to-Image Generative AI Systems
source.authors: Minseon Kim; Hyomin Lee; Boqing Gong; Huishuai Zhang; Sung Ju Hwang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether prompts can evoke concepts after unlearning, but in text-to-image diffusion models rather than LLMs, extending the question to a different modality.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports jailbreak results on commercial text-to-image systems, but those systems are not described as unlearned, so those results are not rows for these claim versions. The unlearning-related evidence is a qualitative prompt comparison in Section 4.3 and figures.
record.test_reason: Applies optimized rephrasing prompts (APGP) to three concept-ablated Stable Diffusion models (Kumari et al. 2023) and reports qualitatively whether erased concepts reappear. This is the version E question in a new setting: text-to-image diffusion rather than LLMs. The evidence is qualitative only (Section 4.3, Figures 11 and 24, Appendix B.5).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that simple defenses, including concept-unlearned models, are inadequate against APGP prompts, which somewhat evoke erased concepts. Evocation is easier, even with human prompts, when the concept strongly correlates with other words, as with Van Gogh. Their main conclusion concerns commercial T2I copyright jailbreaking: 76% violation on ChatGPT with an 11% block rate.
record.recipe_differences: Uses automated prompt optimization and suffixes against text-to-image concept-unlearning models; it does not reproduce the LLM unlearning methods or recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt type matters: APGP-generated prompts somewhat evoke removed concepts, while simple human prompts seem not to. The authors also identify strong associations between a concept and other words as a condition that may make evocation easier.
record.problems: The unlearning results are qualitative, with no numerical recovery measure or uncertainty reported; the paper does not clearly provide per-model results for all three concepts. Evidence is from text-to-image models, not LLMs.
record.rows_left_out: No results on commercial systems without unlearning were included as rows because they do not test recovery after unlearning.

untested.parts: No measurement that the unlearned models reach near-erasure while keeping general generation quality; the paper relies on the cited method.
No activation ablation or internal analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Only optimized English rephrasing prompts in text-to-image diffusion. No LLMs, other languages or in-context information, and no quantitative recovery rate.

missing.what: Concept-dependence finding: for Van Gogh, which correlates with 'star' or 'night', even human prompts may evoke the erased concept, as ours do.

record.verdict_notes: Most of the paper concerns jailbreaking commercial T2I systems with no unlearning, so it is correctly excluded from rows. The unlearning evidence is a short qualitative check on three models from one cited method, with no numbers, controls or uncertainty. Linking to E rests on treating diffusion concept erasure as a new setting for the shallow-unlearning question. A stricter reading of 'same kind of system' (LLMs) would move both rows to none and the finding to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-chance targeted performance while retaining general ability, or test the full claim about attacks after such an outcome.
No fine-tuning or relearning set is used.
No activation direction is ablated and no analysis tests whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests prompts against concept-unlearned text-to-image models, not LLMs; does not test other languages or in-context information.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.check: Recorded as absent, but Appendix B.5 says human prompts may also evoke the erased Van Gogh concept, because it correlates strongly with 'star' or 'night'. The simple-prompt failure therefore holds for the other concepts, with a Van Gogh exception, not uniformly. The concepts are known: R2D2, Monet and Van Gogh. This is a comparator for r1, not an independent result.

relationships.condition: APGP-optimized prompts against Ablating-Concepts Stable Diffusion models (R2D2, Monet, Van Gogh), qualitative judgement
relationships.reason: Optimized prompts only 'somewhat' restore erased concepts (r1), while simple human prompts mostly do not, except for Van Gogh (r2, Appendix B.5). Recovery is partial and depends on prompt optimization and on the concept's word associations.
relationships.display_finding: Optimized prompts produced partial recovery, while simple human prompts mostly failed except for Van Gogh, with success depending on concept-word associations.

relation.reason: Section 4.3 tests whether prompts recover concepts erased by concept unlearning, though only as a small side experiment.

tranche.reason: Concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion is a new setting. The study reports a qualitative result on prompt-only recovery (version E).

source_check.notes: Not an LLM study. The concept-unlearning test is a small qualitative side experiment (Sec 4.3, Figs 11 and 24) with no rates. The main text names the three models (R2D2, Monet, Van Gogh) but cites 'Figure 10a', apparently a typo for 11a. The main results concern copyright jailbreaking of commercial T2I systems.

statements.correction: 2405.16567: three Ablating-Concepts (Kumari et al.) SD models erasing R2D2, Monet, Van Gogh; APGP-optimized prompts somewhat evoke the erased concept; simple human prompts seem to leave it erased, except Van Gogh may be evoked (correlated with star/night; Appendix B.5, Fig 24); qualitative only, no rates; verdict limits_scope, not challenges.
statements.problem: Gives no numbers or claims for this study, but files it under 'against' (robust erasure resists prompt attacks, label challenges). Here APGP prompts 'somewhat evoke' the concept erased by Ablating Concepts: partial recovery, verdict limits_scope. Only the concept-dependence part fits.

statements.correction: 2405.16567 (qualitative, hedged): erased concepts strongly correlated with other words are easier to evoke; Van Gogh (star/night) may come back even with human prompts (Sec 4.3, Appendix B.5, Fig 24). No numbers.
